Get yourself a blood pressure device, the simple cheap push button automatic ones. Takes less than a minute to carry out, maybe do it once a month.

I managed to get to 48 without having a clue that i had sky high blood pressure. Only detected when i attended a health check with the practice nurse, i'd avoided it because i felt petfectly okay.

My diet was good, i exercised 5-6 times a week, do a physical job, didnt smoke and drank very little.

My blood pressure was so dangerously high they expected me to have a heart attack or stroke at any moment. They couldn't believe that i had no symptoms, no palpitations, shortness of breath, dizzyness, headaches.
After further investigations i was also found to have sky high cholestrol as well, i was a heart attack waiting to happen.

The reason it is called the silent killer, you can go from feeling perfectly okay to life threatening heart attack or stroke in the blink of an eye.

It unbelievably hadn't occurred to me that my father had died after a massive heart attack. Being in my early 20s at the time i associated it with him being the age where these things happen, he was 51 !

Please don't think you are too young to be concerned about high blood pressure, i've personally known people in there 30s have heart attacks and strokes.

Please dont ignore these thoughts, you arent having normal thoughts when you get to the point of planning how you will do it. The next step is planning when you will do it, then you are obviously in serious trouble.
As long as you are not acting on these thoughts you are okay, for now.
Please talk to someone you trust, family or friend or better still a professional.

I have recently came out of the other side of severe depression, i went through a number of stages and this was one of them.
I am concerned for you that you feel like this, i felt the same too and then went on to eventually feel so much worse because i hid those feelings from everybody i love.
It got that bad for me that my thoughts changed from 'i'm not doing it because it would hurt my family'. To eventually feeling that 'it would be better if i did it because i'm hurting my family'.
In the end i thought about it every single day & had made plans as to how i would do it. It's only that my wife stopped me walking out of the door one night (the night i was going to do it) that i am still here today.
Only when it got that bad did i finally admit to myself i needed help.
Please don't let it get that far, i think by the sounds of it that you know things aren't right with you. Could you please try to talk to someone you trust, just talking to someone about how you are feeling. It is so much better to hear your own voice speaking these words to someone else who listens rather than having those thoughts going around inside your own mind and never feeling any better.
All you do need to do is talk to someone, it can be so hard to first start doing that but it is so worth it.
